paragraphs.en: A group of Labour MPs, among them Yvette Cooper, are bringing in the new year with a call to institute a UK “town of culture” award. The proposal is that it should sit alongside the existing city of culture title, which was held by Hull in 2017, and has been awarded to Coventry for 2021. Cooper and her colleagues argue that the success of the crown for Hull, where it brought in £220m of investment and an avalanche of arts, ought not to be confined to cities. Britain’s towns, it is true, are not prevented from applying, but they generally lack the resources to put together a bid to beat their bigger competitors. A town of culture award could, it is argued, become an annual event, attracting funding and creating jobs.
paragraphs.zh: 包括伊薇特·库珀在内的一批工党议员以一项倡议迎接新年：设立英国“文化之镇”奖。按照提议，这一奖项应与现有的“文化之城”称号并列；赫尔曾在2017年获得“文化之城”称号，考文垂则已获选为2021年的文化之城。库珀及其同僚认为，这一桂冠为赫尔带来了2.2亿英镑的投资和大量艺术活动，这样的成功不应仅限于城市。诚然，英国的城镇并非不能申报，但它们通常缺乏足够资源，难以组织起能够击败规模更大竞争对手的申报工作。支持者认为，“文化之镇”评选可以成为一年一度的活动，吸引资金并创造就业岗位。

paragraphs.en: Some might see the proposal as a booby prize for the fact that Britain is no longer able to apply for the much more prestigious title of European capital of culture, a sought-after award bagged by Glasgow in 1990 and Liverpool in 2008. A cynic might speculate that the UK is on the verge of disappearing into an endless fever of self-celebration in its desperation to reinvent itself for the post-Brexit world: after town of culture, who knows what will follow-village of culture? Suburb of culture? Hamlet of culture?
paragraphs.zh: 有些人可能会把这一提议看成一种安慰奖，因为英国已无法再申报声望高得多的“欧洲文化之都”称号——这一令人向往的奖项曾于1990年被格拉斯哥、2008年被利物浦收入囊中。持怀疑态度的人也许会揣测：英国急于在脱欧后的世界中重塑自身，是否即将陷入无休止的自我庆祝狂热之中？在“文化之镇”之后，谁知道接下来会是什么——文化之村？文化之郊？文化小村落？

paragraphs.en: It is also wise to recall that such titles are not a cure-all. A badly run “year of culture” washes in and washes out of a place like the tide, bringing prominence for a spell but leaving no lasting benefits to the community. The really successful holders of such titles are those that do a great deal more than fill hotel bedrooms and bring in high-profile arts events and good press for a year. They transform the aspirations of the people who live there; they nudge the self-image of the city into a bolder and more optimistic light. It is hard to get right, and requires a remarkable degree of vision, as well as cooperation between city authorities, the private sector, community groups and cultural organisations. But it can be done: Glasgow's year as European capital of culture can certainly be seen as one of a complex series of factors that have turned the city into the powerhouse of art, music and theatre that it remains today.
paragraphs.zh: 明智的做法还包括记住：此类称号并非包治百病的良药。组织不善的“文化年”会像潮水一样在一个地方涌来又退去，让它一时声名鹊起，却不会为当地社区留下持久的益处。真正成功的获奖城市所做的，远远不止让酒店客房住满、在一年里引进备受瞩目的艺术活动、赢得媒体好评。它们会改变当地居民的志向，使城市对自身的认知变得更有胆识、更为乐观。要把这件事做好并不容易，既需要非凡的远见，也需要市政府、私营部门、社区团体和文化机构相互合作。但这完全可以做到：格拉斯哥担任欧洲文化之都的那一年，无疑可以被视为一系列复杂因素中的一个；这些因素共同使它成为艺术、音乐和戏剧重镇，并将这一地位保持至今。

paragraphs.en: A “town of culture” could be not just about the arts but about honouring a town’s peculiarities—helping sustain its high street, supporting local facilities and above all celebrating its people. Jeremy Wright, the culture secretary, should welcome this positive, hope-filled proposal, and tum it into action.
paragraphs.zh: “文化之镇”可以不仅关乎艺术，还关乎彰显一座城镇的独特之处——帮助维持其商业街的活力，支持当地设施，尤其是赞颂当地人民。文化大臣杰里米·赖特应当欢迎这一积极而充满希望的提议，并将其付诸行动。
